summary:
SARWISE – See the Invisible. Understand the Change.

SARWISE is an interactive Earth-change monitoring platform designed to transform complex NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations into meaningful environmental insights. We propose a user-friendly dashboard that allows users to explore surface changes through interactive maps, multi-date satellite comparisons and visual change analysis.

Our initial focus is the Kuttanad–Vembanad region of Kerala, where we aim to demonstrate how SAR data can help identify changes in water coverage, flood inundation patterns and wetland boundaries. Key features include Flood Vision, Wetland Watch, an interactive Earth Time Machine and Change Intelligence, which highlights changing areas and estimates their spatial extent.

By leveraging NISAR's L-band and S-band radar capabilities, SARWISE addresses the challenge of monitoring Earth's surface even through clouds and in darkness. It bridges the gap between advanced satellite data and practical understanding, supporting environmental researchers, farmers and decision-makers. Our vision is to make satellite-based change detection more accessible, understandable and useful for protecting ecosystems and communities worldwide.
details: SARWISE – See the Invisible. Understand the Change. 1. Project Overview SARWISE is an interactive Earth-change monitoring platform designed to transform complex NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations into meaningful environmental insights. It helps users identify, visualize and understand changes occurring on Earth's surface, with an initial focus on flood-related water coverage and wetland transformation in Kerala's Kuttanad–Vembanad region. Traditional optical satellites can face difficulties observing Earth's surface during cloudy weather and at night. SAR technology overcomes these limitations by using radar signals to observe the Earth's surface through clouds and in darkness. SARWISE aims to make this powerful technology accessible through an intuitive, interactive platform. 2. How Does It Work? SARWISE follows a satellite-to-insight workflow: 1. Data Acquisition: Obtain NISAR radar observations and relevant supporting geospatial datasets. 2. Data Processing: Prepare radar imagery using appropriate techniques such as calibration, speckle filtering, terrain correction and geospatial alignment. 3. Change Detection: Compare observations from different dates using radar backscatter information to identify changes in surface conditions. 4. Visualization: Display detected changes through interactive maps, colour-coded layers and before-and-after comparisons. 5. Analysis: Estimate the spatial extent of detected changes and highlight areas that may require further investigation. Users can select geographical locations, explore available observation dates and compare how the Earth's surface has changed over time. 3. Main Features SARWISE combines five important capabilities: - Flood Vision: Visualizes changes in water-covered areas and helps identify potential flood-inundation zones. - Wetland Watch: Monitors changes in wetland boundaries, water bodies and surrounding land. - Earth Time Machine: Provides an interactive timeline to compare satellite observations from different dates. - Change Intelligence: Highlights detected changes using colour-coded maps and estimates their geographical extent. - Community Impact: Presents satellite-derived information in an understandable format for farmers, researchers and local authorities. 4. Benefits and Intended Impact Our initial focus is Kuttanad, Kerala, where water distribution, wetlands and agriculture are closely connected. SARWISE aims to support environmental awareness and research by making changes easier to observe and interpret. The platform can help researchers study wetland transformation, provide agricultural communities with useful information about changing water conditions and support local authorities in identifying areas requiring further investigation. In the future, SARWISE can be expanded to applications such as deforestation monitoring, agricultural assessment, soil-moisture studies, glacier monitoring and land-surface deformation. It is designed as a monitoring and decision-support tool, not an operational flood forecasting or emergency-warning system. 5. Tools and Technologies Our proposed development stack includes Python for SAR processing and data analysis, JavaScript and React for the interactive interface, FastAPI for backend services, Leaflet or MapLibre for geographical visualization, ESA SNAP for radar processing, and Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy, SciPy and Plotly for geospatial analysis and visualization. NISAR is the primary satellite data source. Supplementary datasets such as Sentinel-1 may be used where necessary and will be clearly distinguished. 6. Creativity and Innovation The uniqueness of SARWISE lies in converting complex radar observations into understandable environmental information. Features such as the Earth Time Machine, interactive before-and-after explorer and Change Intelligence make satellite-based monitoring more intuitive and engaging. Our team considered scientific reliability, data availability, usability, environmental relevance and scalability. We also considered the influence of surface moisture, roughness, vegetation and observation geometry on radar backscatter to avoid misleading interpretations. Our Vision: To bridge the gap between advanced satellite technology and real-world environmental understanding. Team Seblaski: Nirmal C George, P Pranav Krishnan, Neeraj Pallakkat and Gokul Arun Menon.
